item.title: Snowball! — Mon Aug 24, 8:30 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group Beginning at Beetree Gap near the Craggy picnic area, we’ll follow the trail north into the western Great Craggy Mountains. The trail follows a high ridge in the Big Ivy region of Pisgah National Forest. A highlight of the hike is Hawkbill Rock, an exposed peak with wide-ranging views of the Elk Mountains. **This area is a bit of a scramble**. The trail then continues north along a wide ridge. The terminus of the trail is the site of a former lookout tower.
Snowball is 3.5 miles out and access to the trail from the intersection of Bee Tree Gap and the BRP is 0.5 miles. **Out and back is approximately 8 miles.** The trail profile includes hiking up to Snowball Mtn., then down to Hawkbill Rock, and beyond that down to Snowball Gap, then up to Little Snowball Mtn., and finally up to the site of Little Snowball fire tower. **Total elevation is over 2,000 feet.**
Like most of our summer hikes at elevation, **this is not an easy hike**. You will be fatigued. Hiki

item.description:
Ben Balmer, raised in Ypsilanti, Michigan, started his musical journey with the harmonica at 13, quickly adding guitar and performing in clubs by age 16. item.title: Fall Wildflowers of the NC Arboretum — Wed Sep 9, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Fall Wildflowers of the NC Arboretum with Lauren Lampley Wednesday, September 9 | 1 – 4pm BRN – Core | BREG – Core Register Here!
Interested in learning how to identify wildflowers? Join Lauren on this walk around the Arboretum property where we will go over different ways of identifying plants and different families of flowers. Some flowers are very difficult to identify to species and some are relatively easy so we will talk about how to get as close as possible with tools we can easily carry into the field. We will be using Newcomb’s guide to key out some of the less common flowers but will focus on learning how to look closely at flowers to identify them. This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. item.description:
AVL Writers This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.
For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.
Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.
If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.
If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).

item.title: Manifesting Self — Thu Sep 24, 6:00 PM
item.description:
AVL Digital Nomads **Location Change:** **Disclaimer: In all efforts to keep this Meetup a safe space, we all agree to keep anything said within the group private and confidential.**
Do you want to take your remote working game to the next level? Do you find yourself saying wtf is Manifesting Self??
Well, you’re not alone. Remote working is glamorous, and also presents itself with challenges not seen in the traditional office environment.
Manifesting Self may sound a little out there. Trust me. It’s not. Whether we’ve been in the remote space for years, since the pandemic, or just recently, I’m certain it has changed each of us in ways we never thought possible. Let’s explore that together. The highs, the lows, and everywhere in between. And from there experience growth.
We are so excited to see you, again or for the first time!
Source: AVL Digital Nomads
